lines.text: Spider silk beats steel. Pound for pound.
But one spider's silk is almost unfair.
A single strand is much thinner than a human hair.
Yet for its weight, it can hold more than steel wire before it snaps.
And some silk stretches up to four times its length without breaking.
lines.caption: And some silk stretches up to 4× its length without breaking.

lines.text: Now meet Darwin's bark spider, from Madagascar. It hangs webs over rivers on lines up to twenty-five meters long.
lines.caption: Now meet Darwin's bark spider, from Madagascar. It hangs webs over rivers on lines up to 25 meters long.

lines.text: Its silk is about ten times tougher than Kevlar.
lines.caption: Its silk is about 10× tougher than Kevlar.

lines.text: Sounds fake? It's true. Follow for more.
